title: Quant-profile rollback policy and diagnostics for explainable schema failures under low-bit inference
creator: Liam Chen
description: Define and implement an automated rollback and diagnostics workflow for FP8/INT8 model variants when structured outputs violate JSON schemas or function-call contracts. The goal is to (1) automatically detect repeatable schema regressions in production, (2) collect explainable per-request artifacts to triage whether failures are syntactic (parse) vs semantic (field value corruption), and (3) execute a safe fallback to a higher-precision variant (FP16 or a validated INT8 profile) while preserving observability and low false-positive rate. This work spans runtime policy, telemetry schema, CI fuzzing harness, and a Console dashboard with actionable signals for PM/Support.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime rollback policy: configurable rule that triggers fallback after configurable threshold (default: 5 schema-failing requests from same route in 60s) and reverts automatically when failure rate drops below threshold for 15m

Per-request diagnostic bundle: includes model profile used, quantization metadata (scale/zero-point or FP8 exponent), tokenized prefix snapshot, top-10 logit delta vs FP16 baseline, serialized output, parse error type (syntactic|semantic|missing-field|type-mismatch), and a small normalized diff (Levenshtein or JSON-structure distance)
CI-grade regression detector: harness that runs structured-output fuzzing over golden prompt set and flags regression >=2% schema-violation rate vs baseline FP16 for any quant profile

Failure classifier: lightweight heuristic model that labels failures as 'recoverable' (fallback to FP16 expected to fix) or 'investigate' (semantic degradation), with >=85% precision on labeled validation set
Console integration: dashboard tile showing per-route schema violation rate, recent rollback events, and link to diagnostic archives; allow manual 'pin FP16' from UI for the affected route
Runbook & tests: documented runbook for support + end-to-end tests that simulate production traffic patterns including KV-cache warm/cold transitions and batched requests
tasks: Design telemetry schema for diagnostic bundle and agree on retention/cost trade-offs with Observability team
Instrument runtime to emit per-request schema-check outcome and attach diagnostic bundle on failure (size-capped, async upload)
Implement policy engine for thresholding and safe rollback with rate-limited retries and cooldown windows
Build failure-classifier prototype (rules + lightweight model) and curate labeled dataset from calibration experiments
Extend CI fuzzing harness to spawn quantized runtime instances and compare outputs against FP16 golden baseline
Expose rollback / violation signals in Console, add a 'rollback history' view and one-click pin-to-FP16
Create runbook and add automated alerting (PagerDuty) for persistent regressions and manual escalation path
comments: 2025-02-13 | Liam Chen: Initial spike complete. Measured schema-failure patterns on a 10k sample from nightly calibration runs. Failures cluster into short serialized parse errors and field-value truncations in numeric fields. Gathered candidate telemetry fields.

2025-02-18 | Aisha Patel: Design review with Observability and Security. Agreed to limit per-request diagnostic uploads to 2KB compressed by default and gate full payloads behind sampling + opt-in for enterprise customers. Observability prefers async S3-style archive with signed links in traces.

2025-02-22 | Tomás Rivera (Infra): Prototype policy engine added to runtime branch 'quant-rollback-v1'. It supports windowed counters and cooldown; still missing safe retry/backoff semantics and persistence across process restarts.

2025-02-26 | QA: Fuzz harness run (3k seeds) against int8-profile A produced 2.8% schema violations vs FP16 baseline; many were recoverable syntactic issues after adding a small tokenization tweak. Created dataset 'quant-failures-2025-02-26' in gs://redwood-quant-results/.

2025-03-01 | Aisha Patel: Added acceptance criteria for failure classifier precision. Proposed default rollback threshold: 5 fails in 60s for production routes, opt-down to 2 fails for high-priority routes (admins can tune).

2025-03-03 | Liam Chen: Implemented diagnostic bundle builder and async uploader. PR opened: https://github.com/redwoodinc/runtime/pull/1427. Running end-to-end test against a synthetic Chat API route; initial results look promising (rollback triggered correctly, console shows event).
